limitations: Discrete local leg samples do not establish continuous clearance or full robot clearance.
Connector proxies are provisional envelopes and do not reproduce flexible cable behavior.
The blind connector pocket leaves about 1.6 mm of material; fit and loaded strength require physical tests.
Printed tolerances, loaded deflection, retainer seating and servo thermal behavior remain physical checks.
Tool envelopes establish access only for their specified dimensions and approach directions.

motion.scope: Twenty-seven local leg poses; same-link pairs are excluded from motion checking

connector_reserves.scope: Three critical poses at yaw zero; each proxy is checked against every part except its owning servo
connector_reserves.limitation: The proxy is a provisional plugged-profile and wire reserve, not a measured cable sweep

clamp_access.scope: Nine clamp screw and tool paths in one complete local leg at one assembly pose.
limitations: Results apply to this pose and these explicit proxy dimensions only.
All supplied physical solids are tested, including servo cases, horns and discs; none is exempted for sharing a link.
Current leg geometry does not include clamp fasteners or central retainers. Their real dimensions and seating need confirmation.
The screw assumes a bare seated M3 x 35 cap head. Washers, a different head, nut or screw length change the envelopes.
The nut insertion starts at raw Y=-25 mm, matching the opened access passage; initial nut positioning outside that entry is not swept.
The matched hex envelope allows normal captive-nut flats. It does not prove printed fit or resistance to nut rotation under tightening.
The hollow nut holder clears a projecting screw but is an assumed aid; it does not establish how a real tool holds the nut.
The driver checks a straight exposed shaft at the seated head. Driver handles, hand clearance and the whole driver insertion motion are absent.
The local leg test omits the body, neighboring legs, ground, flexible wiring and unmodeled connectors.
Touching surfaces and positive intersections below the reporting threshold are retained in the report and require interpretation.
No blocking volume above threshold is not a physical access verification or a tolerance allowance.

retention.retention_logic: The screw and washer tighten onto the fixed stub. The washer overlaps the disc bore while remaining axially clear of the rotating disc.
limitations: The 1.6 mm blind floor is nominal remaining material, not a verified load capacity.
Measure the actual stub, disc bore and washer before confirming free rotation.
The retaining screw head and thread engagement are not modeled by this washer check.
A compatible supplier shell is used; it is not certified as the exact owned C018 build.

original_clamp_access_diagnostic: The original clamp_access section used a bare screw head. Its measurements and failures are preserved. Use actual_washer_clamp_access for the planned 0.5 mm head washer stack.

actual_washer_clamp_access.scope: All original full-leg screw and tool checks with the actual head-washer offset, plus nine seated head washers. Nut tool paths are unchanged.
limitations: All supplied physical leg parts remain in the obstruction test, including neighboring moving links.
Nut insertion and holder paths are unchanged from the original report, so staged preload does not hide service-access obstructions.
The washer is checked seated; the route used to place it under the screw head is not swept.
The driver remains a 3 mm straight shaft with 40 mm exposed length at the seated head; handles and hand clearance are absent.
The M3 x 35 screw assumes a 5.5 mm diameter, 3 mm tall head. Actual screw dimensions and thread engagement need confirmation.
The complete local leg is checked at one pose; the body, neighboring legs, flexible wiring and unmodeled connectors are absent.
No blocking volume above threshold does not establish physical access or a manufacturing tolerance allowance.

staged_nut_assembly.scope: Continuous entry of all nine nuts into bare printed carriers, followed by seated hardware checks with each carrier's own servo and cap.
procedure: Preload the bare yaw saddle, hip coxa carrier and knee femur carrier before installing their servos or caps. Keep the hip lower arm, surrounding femur and tibia assemblies absent. The hip carrier's integrated post remains present.

For all yaw nuts, the hip rear nut and all knee nuts, align the nut flats to the printed trap and feed from the open negative raw-Y side. The checked continuous entry begins with the nut rear face at raw Y=-60 mm and ends at Y=-16.1 mm.
For the hip front lower nut at raw X=13.915, Z=-23 mm, hold its thickness at raw Y=-20 to -17.6 mm and slide its center from raw Z=-40 to -23 mm through the side opening.
For the hip front upper nut at raw X=13.915, Z=-7 mm, hold the same raw-Y thickness interval and slide its center from raw Z=5 to -7 mm through the opposite side opening.

After either hip front nut reaches its bolt axis, translate it 3.9 mm along positive raw Y. Its seated interval is Y=-16.1 to -13.7 mm. This lateral-then-axial route avoids assuming the nut starts inside the reopened channel.

Keep each nut seated while installing its servo and cap. Place a 0.5 mm OD7/ID3.2 head washer under each M3 x 35 screw, then engage the nut from the cap side before fitting surrounding leg assemblies.
For later hip nut removal or replacement, remove surrounding parts to recover the bare-carrier access used here. The original assembled-leg nut-tool obstructions remain reported separately.
limitations: Entry sweeps use a filled nut exterior, conservatively including its thread hole. Seated nuts use a simple 3 mm bore; thread geometry and tightening are not simulated.
The nominal matching-flat clearance is 0.1 mm per side and needs a printed fit check.
The checks establish a route for the nut itself, not clearance for fingers, a wrench or a particular nut-holding tool.
Keeping a loose nut seated during servo and cap installation remains a physical assembly task.
Servo and cap insertion motions are not swept; their final seated relationship to the nuts, screws and washers is checked.
These staged checks deliberately exclude the body, lower arm and surrounding moving links before they are fitted. They do not replace the full assembled-leg service-access report.
Physical fit, plastic deformation, washer tolerances and thread engagement remain unverified.
Input parts must come from the production build matching the recorded sources. Before/after hashes detect file changes during this check, not the caller's earlier shape construction.

top_level_passed_meaning: This separate addendum evaluates the verified preload procedure. The original strict complete-assembly report is preserved unchanged at original_report_path.

staged_addendum_provenance.motion_reuse_basis: Every original checker and geometry source hash still matches the completed 27-pose report
